claims.text: Machine-learning phase-prediction models can be applied to multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Atomic-size difference and valence-electron concentration can be used to describe phase distribution in high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning models can predict phase distributions accurately in high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning phase-prediction models can accurately predict high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
Machine-learning phase-prediction models can make materials exploration more efficient.
The intervention will improve the accuracy of transition-temperature determination relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve the determination of fusion enthalpy.
The intervention will improve the determination of fusion entropy.
The intervention will improve the determination of solid-to-fluid volume change.
The intervention will improve the determination of dense-fluid heat capacity.
The intervention will be more efficient than DFT free-energy studies and TOR-TILD.
The proposed approach is limited to high-entropy alloys containing multiple principal elements.
Model accuracy may depend on the quality and quantity of training data.
The machine-learning models may fail to capture all thermodynamic effects relevant to the solid-to-fluid transition.
A comparison against experimental and computational benchmarks can test the model using transition temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity.
